import pandas as pd
from functools import reduce

# Read files (no path needed)
df1 = pd.read_excel("state_sales_no_taxes_tips.csv.xlsx")
df2 = pd.read_excel("state_sales_per_capita_no_taxes_tips.csv.xlsx")
df3 = pd.read_excel("state_sales_per_capita_with_taxes_tips.csv.xlsx")
df4 = pd.read_excel("state_sales_with_taxes_tips.csv.xlsx")

# Put all dataframes in a list
dfs = [df1, df2, df3, df4]

# Loop through each dataframe and clean up its column names i.e., Standardize column names
for df in dfs:
    df.columns = df.columns.str.strip().str.lower()

# Merge all at once on year and state
merged_df = reduce(
    lambda l, r: pd.merge(l, r, on=["year", "state"], how="inner"),
    dfs
)

merged_df.head()
#to create the file in the folder
merged_df.to_csv("merged_state_sales_panel.csv", index=False)
merged_df.columns

import pandas as pd

# 1. Load the dataset
Tax= 'merged_state_sales_panel.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(Tax)

# ---- Filter for years 2020-2024 ---
df = df[df['year'].between(2020, 2025)]

# 2. Define the exact column names from the USDA dataset
fafh_with_tax = 'food-away-from-home sales with taxes and tips (millions of nominal u.s. dollars)'
fafh_no_tax = 'food-away-from-home sales without taxes and tips (millions of nominal u.s. dollars)'
fah_with_tax = 'food-at-home sales with taxes and tips (millions of nominal u.s. dollars)'
fah_no_tax = 'food-at-home sales without taxes and tips (millions of nominal u.s. dollars)'

# 3. Calculate the FAFH tax rate (Ad-Valorem formula)
df['fafh_tax_rate'] = ((df[fafh_with_tax] - df[fafh_no_tax]) / df[fafh_no_tax])*100

# 4.  Calculate the FAH tax rate (Ad-Valorem formula)
df['fah_tax_rate'] = ((df[fah_with_tax] - df[fah_no_tax]) / df[fah_no_tax])*100

# 5. Save the updated DataFrame to an Excel workbook
output_file = 'merged_state_sales_panel.xlsx' 
df.to_excel(output_file, index=False)

# 6. Print the first few rows to verify the calculation
print(df.head(10))

# 8. Save the updated DataFrame to an Excel workbook
output_file = 'merged_state_sales_panel.csv' 
df.to_csv(output_file, index=False)

import pandas as pd

import os

##Create combined demographic dataset with variables selected
columns_to_keep = ['GESTFIPS', 'HRYEAR4','PRTAGE', 'PESEX', 'PTDTRACE', 'PEEDUCA', 'PEMARITL','HRPOOR','PRNMCHLD', 'GTMETSTA','GESTFIPS','PREMPNOT','HETENURE','PUDIS',
                   'PRCITSHP','HESP1','HETS8O']
rename_map = {
    'HRYEAR4': 'Year',
    'GESTFIPS': 'State',
    'PRTAGE': 'Age',
    'PESEX': 'Sex',
    'PTDTRACE': 'Race',
    'PEMARITL': 'Marriage',
    'PEEDUCA': 'Education',
    'HRPOOR': 'Poverty',
    'PRNMCHLD': 'Children',
    'GTMETSTA': 'Metropolitan_Status',
    'PREMPNOT': 'Employment',
    'HETENURE': 'Living_Quarter_Status',
    'PRCITSHP': 'Citizenship',
    'HETS8O': 'Food_Expenditure_Last_Week'
}

all_dfs = []

for year in range(2020, 2025):

    yy = str(year)[-2:]
    filename = f"dec{yy}pub.csv"
    
    if os.path.exists(filename):
        print(f"Reading {filename}...")
        
        data = pd.read_csv(filename, usecols=columns_to_keep)
        
        data = data.rename(columns=rename_map)
        # Add to our list
        all_dfs.append(data)
    else:
        print(f"Warning: {filename} not found.")

if all_dfs:
    master_panel = pd.concat(all_dfs, ignore_index=True)
    
    # Preview the data
    print("\nMaster dataset created successfully!")
    print(master_panel.head())
    
    # 4. Save the combined file
    master_panel.to_csv("combined_demographics_20_24.csv", index=False)
else:
    print("No files were processed.")

demo = pd.read_csv('combined_demographics_20_24.csv')
demo.columns
demo.shape

import pandas as pd

name_to_code_map = {
    'Alabama': '1', 'Alaska': '2', 'Arizona': '4', 'Arkansas': '5', 'California': '6',
    'Colorado': '8', 'Connecticut': '9', 'Delaware': '10', 'District of Columbia': '11',
    'Florida': '12', 'Georgia': '13', 'Hawaii': '15', 'Idaho': '16', 'Illinois': '17',
    'Indiana': '18', 'Iowa': '19', 'Kansas': '20', 'Kentucky': '21', 'Louisiana': '22',
    'Maine': '23', 'Maryland': '24', 'Massachusetts': '25', 'Michigan': '26', 'Minnesota': '27',
    'Mississippi': '28', 'Missouri': '29', 'Montana': '30', 'Nebraska': '31', 'Nevada': '32',
    'New Hampshire': '33', 'New Jersey': '34', 'New Mexico': '35', 'New York': '36',
    'North Carolina': '37', 'North Dakota': '38', 'Ohio': '39', 'Oklahoma': '40',
    'Oregon': '41', 'Pennsylvania': '42', 'Rhode Island': '44', 'South Carolina': '45',
    'South Dakota': '46', 'Tennessee': '47', 'Texas': '48', 'Utah': '49', 'Vermont': '50',
    'Virginia': '51', 'Washington': '53', 'West Virginia': '54', 'Wisconsin': '55', 'Wyoming': '56'
}

# Only Tax needs the name→FIPS mapping — Demographics are already numeric
Tax['State'] = Tax['State'].map(name_to_code_map)

# Standardize types across all three
for df_ref in [Tax, Demographics]:
    df_ref['State'] = pd.to_numeric(df_ref['State'], errors='coerce')
    df_ref['Year'] = pd.to_numeric(df_ref['Year'], errors='coerce')

print(f"Tax NaN State: {Tax['State'].isna().sum()}")
print(f"Demographics NaN State: {Demographics['State'].isna().sum()}")

# Trim Tax down to just what you need
Tax = Tax[['Year', 'State', 'fafh_tax_rate', 'fah_tax_rate']]

# Merge: Demographics (base) + Tax 
combined_df = pd.merge(Demographics, Tax, on=['State', 'Year'], how='left')
print(f"After Tax merge (should ≈ 638,589 rows): {combined_df.shape}")

combined_df.to_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv', index=False)
print(f"Total rows: {len(combined_df):,}")

print(combined_df[['fafh_tax_rate', 'fah_tax_rate']].isna().sum())

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load  dataset
df_cleaned = pd.read_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv')
# DEMOGRAPHIC VARIABLES 

# MARRIAGE values: 
# -1 -> NaN (Empty cell)
#1, 2 -> 1
# 3, 4, 5, 6 -> 2
marriage_map = {-1: np.nan, 1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 2, 4: 2, 5: 2, 6: 2}
df_cleaned['Marriage'] = df_cleaned['Marriage'].map(marriage_map)

# If RACE is 1, 2, or 4, keep it. 
# If RACE is  3 and between 5 and 26, change to 0.
mask = (df_cleaned['Race'] == 3) | ((df_cleaned['Race'] >= 5) & (df_cleaned['Race'] <= 26))
df_cleaned['Race'] = np.where(mask, 0, df_cleaned['Race'])
df_cleaned['Race'] = df_cleaned['Race'].replace({-1: np.nan})

# COLLEGE DEGREE (Convert -1 to NaN first without affecting other numbers)
df_cleaned['Education'] = df_cleaned['Education'].replace(-1, np.nan)
conditions = [
    (df_cleaned['Education'] >= 31) & (df_cleaned['Education'] <= 40),
    (df_cleaned['Education'] >= 41) & (df_cleaned['Education'] <= 46)
]
choices = [1, 2] # 1 for No Degree, 2 for Degree
df_cleaned['Education'] = np.select(conditions, choices, default=df_cleaned['Education'])

# AGE
df_cleaned['Age'] = df_cleaned['Age'].replace({0: np.nan, -1: np.nan})

# DISABILITY
df_cleaned['Disability'] = df_cleaned['Disability'].replace({-1: np.nan , -2: np.nan , -3: np.nan, 3:2})

# EMPLOYMENT
df_cleaned['Employment'] = df_cleaned['Employment'].replace({-1: np.nan, 4: 3})

#BENEFITS
df_cleaned['Benefits'] = df_cleaned['Benefits'].replace({-1: np.nan,  -2: np.nan , -3: np.nan , -9: np.nan})

#CITIZENSHIP
df_cleaned['Citizenship'] = df_cleaned['Citizenship'].replace({2: 1, 3: 1 , 4: 1 , 5: 0})
df_cleaned['Citizenship'] = df_cleaned['Citizenship'].replace({-1: np.nan})

# METROPOLITAN STATUS 
df_cleaned['Metropolitan_Status'] = df_cleaned['Metropolitan_Status'].replace({3: np.nan})

# POVERTY
df_cleaned['Poverty'] = df_cleaned['Poverty'].replace({
    -1: np.nan})

df_cleaned.to_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv', index=False)



# Loop through the columns and print the distribution of each
for col in ['Age', 'Race', 'Education', 'Disability', 'Employment', 'Marriage', 'Citizenship', 'Poverty',
            'Metropolitan_Status',  'Benefits']:
    print(f"--- {col} Value Counts ---")
    print(df_cleaned[col].value_counts().sort_index())
    print("\n")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# 1. Load the cleaned data
final = pd.read_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv')

# 2. Wipe out the invalid answers for food expenditure
# Filtering between $8 and $600 based on your criteria
df_cleaned = final[(final['Food_Expenditure_Last_Week'] >= 8) & 
                   (final['Food_Expenditure_Last_Week'] <= 600)].copy()

# 3. Create the new log expenditure column
# We use np.log() for the natural logarithm
df_cleaned['Log_Food_Expenditure_Last_Week'] = np.log(df_cleaned['Food_Expenditure_Last_Week'])

# 4. Save the final version
df_cleaned.to_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv', index=False)
df_cleaned.columns

import pandas as pd
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH

# 0. CLEAN AND SAVE DATA -------------------------------------------------

# Assume df already exists in memory
df = df[df['fah_tax_rate'] >= 0].copy()
df = df.dropna().copy()
df.to_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv', index=False)

# 1. LOAD AND SETUP ------------------------------------------------------

df = pd.read_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv')

vars_for_table = [
    'Age', 'Race', 'Education', 'Marriage', 'Disability',
    'Employment', 'Sex', 'Living_Quarter_Status', 'Metropolitan_Status',
    'Citizenship', 'Children', 'Poverty',
    'Food_Expenditure_Last_Week', 'Log_Food_Expenditure_Last_Week',
    'fafh_tax_rate', 'fah_tax_rate'
]

labels = {
    'Race': {1: 'White', 2: 'Black', 4: 'Asian', 0: 'Mixed'},
    'Education': {1.0: 'No College Degree', 2.0: 'College Degree'},
    'Marriage': {1.0: 'Married', 2.0: 'Not Married'},
    'Employment': {1.0: 'Employed', 2.0: 'Unemployed', 3.0: 'Not in labour force'},
    'Sex': {1: 'Male', 2: 'Female'},
    'Living_Quarter_Status': {1: 'Owned', 2: 'Rented', 3: 'Occupied'},
    'Metropolitan_Status': {1: 'Metro', 2: 'Non-Metro'},
    'Citizenship': {1: 'Citizen', 0: 'Non-Citizen'},
    'Poverty': {1: 'Below 185% Poverty', 2: 'Above 185% Poverty'}
}

continuous_vars = [
    'Age', 'Children', 'Food_Expenditure_Last_Week',
    'Log_Food_Expenditure_Last_Week', 'fafh_tax_rate',
    'fah_tax_rate'
]

categorical_vars = [
    'Race', 'Education', 'Marriage', 
    'Employment', 'Sex', 'Living_Quarter_Status',
    'Metropolitan_Status', 'Citizenship',
    'Poverty']

# 2. BUILD SUMMARY TABLE -------------------------------------------------

table_data = []

# total N row
total_obs = len(df)
table_data.append(['Observations', f'{total_obs:,}', '—', '—', '—', '—'])

for var in vars_for_table:
    if var not in df.columns:
        continue

    if var in continuous_vars:
        res = df[var].agg(['count', 'mean', 'std', 'min', 'max'])
        table_data.append([
            var,
            f'{int(res["count"]):,}',
            f'{res["mean"]:.2f}',
            f'{res["std"]:.2f}',
            f'{res["min"]:.2f}',
            f'{res["max"]:.2f}'
        ])

    elif var in categorical_vars:
        total_n = df[var].notna().sum()
        table_data.append([var, f'{int(total_n):,}', '—', '—', '—', '—'])

        counts = df[var].value_counts().sort_index()
        for code, n in counts.items():
            if var in labels:
                text_label = labels[var].get(code, f'Code {code}')
            else:
                text_label = f'Code {code}'

            pct = n / total_n if total_n > 0 else 0
            table_data.append([
                f'  {text_label}',
                f'{int(n):,}',
                f'{pct:.3f}',
                '—', '—', '—'
            ])

# 3. PRINT SUMMARY TABLE TO CONSOLE ------------------------------------
headers = ['Variable', 'N', 'Mean/Pct', 'Std Dev', 'Min', 'Max']

# Calculate column widths dynamically
col_widths = [max(len(str(row[i])) for row in [headers] + table_data) for i in range(len(headers))]

# Print header
header_row = '  '.join(str(headers[i]).ljust(col_widths[i]) for i in range(len(headers)))
separator  = '  '.join('-' * col_widths[i] for i in range(len(headers)))

print("\n" + "=" * len(separator))
print("SUMMARY STATISTICS TABLE")
print("=" * len(separator))
print(header_row)
print(separator)

# Print rows
for row in table_data:
    print('  '.join(str(row[i]).ljust(col_widths[i]) for i in range(len(row))))

print("=" * len(separator))
print(f"Total Observations: {total_obs:,}")
print("=" * len(separator))

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import numpy as np

# Load data
df_plot = pd.read_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv')

# Name to code mapping
name_to_code_map = {
    'Alabama': '1', 'Alaska': '2', 'Arizona': '4', 'Arkansas': '5', 'California': '6',
    'Colorado': '8', 'Connecticut': '9', 'Delaware': '10', 'District of Columbia': '11',
    'Florida': '12', 'Georgia': '13', 'Hawaii': '15', 'Idaho': '16', 'Illinois': '17',
    'Indiana': '18', 'Iowa': '19', 'Kansas': '20', 'Kentucky': '21', 'Louisiana': '22',
    'Maine': '23', 'Maryland': '24', 'Massachusetts': '25', 'Michigan': '26', 'Minnesota': '27',
    'Mississippi': '28', 'Missouri': '29', 'Montana': '30', 'Nebraska': '31', 'Nevada': '32',
    'New Hampshire': '33', 'New Jersey': '34', 'New Mexico': '35', 'New York': '36',
    'North Carolina': '37', 'North Dakota': '38', 'Ohio': '39', 'Oklahoma': '40',
    'Oregon': '41', 'Pennsylvania': '42', 'Rhode Island': '44', 'South Carolina': '45',
    'South Dakota': '46', 'Tennessee': '47', 'Texas': '48', 'Utah': '49', 'Vermont': '50',
    'Virginia': '51', 'Washington': '53', 'West Virginia': '54', 'Wisconsin': '55', 'Wyoming': '56'
}

# Reverse mapping: code → full name
code_to_name = {v: k for k, v in name_to_code_map.items()}

# CHART 2b: Boxplot - Food Expenditure distribution by State (alphabetical order)
grouped = df_plot.groupby('State')['Food_Expenditure_Last_Week']
state_data_raw = [(state, grp.dropna().values) for state, grp in grouped]

# Sort ALPHABETICALLY by full state name
state_data_sorted = sorted(state_data_raw, key=lambda x: code_to_name.get(str(x[0]), str(x[0])))
labels = [code_to_name.get(str(s), str(s)) for s, _ in state_data_sorted]
data   = [d for _, d in state_data_sorted]

# Overall reference lines
all_vals = df_plot['Food_Expenditure_Last_Week'].dropna()
overall_median = np.median(all_vals)
overall_q1 = np.percentile(all_vals, 25)
overall_q3 = np.percentile(all_vals, 75)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(26, 12))  # Wider to accommodate full state names

bp = ax.boxplot(
    data,
    tick_labels=labels,
    showfliers=False,
    patch_artist=True,
    whis=1.5,
    medianprops=dict(color='darkred', linewidth=2.5)
)

# Brighter box colors
for patch in bp['boxes']:
    patch.set_facecolor('#4DA8DA')
    patch.set_alpha(0.8)

# Add reference lines
ax.axhline(
    overall_median,
    color='darkred',
    linestyle='--',
    linewidth=2,
    label=f'Overall Median: ${overall_median:.0f}'
)
ax.axhline(
    overall_q1,
    color='#1f77b4',
    linestyle=':',
    linewidth=1.5,
    label=f'Overall Q1: ${overall_q1:.0f}'
)
ax.axhline(
    overall_q3,
    color='#1f77b4',
    linestyle=':',
    linewidth=1.5,
    label=f'Overall Q3: ${overall_q3:.0f}'
)

# Formatting
ax.set_title(
    'Figure 2: Food Expenditure Distribution by State',
    fontsize=20,
    fontweight='bold',
    loc='left',
    pad=30
)
ax.set_xlabel('State', fontsize=16)
ax.set_ylabel('Weekly Food Expenditure ($)', fontsize=16)
ax.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=16, rotation=90)  # 90° = vertical text
ax.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=24)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'${x:,.0f}'))
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Legend
handles, labels_legend = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
by_label = dict(zip(labels_legend, handles))
ax.legend(
    by_label.values(),
    by_label.keys(),
    fontsize=24,
    framealpha=0.95,
    edgecolor='black',
    fancybox=True,
    loc='upper right'
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('Distribution_by_State_Boxplot.png', dpi=600, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
plt.show()
plt.close(fig)

# Exclude raw Food_Expenditure to avoid redundancy with the Log version
vif_exclude = ['Food_Expenditure_Last_Week']
vif_vars = [v for v in vars_for_table if v not in vif_exclude and v in df.columns]

# Separate to identify what needs dummy encoding
cont_vif = [v for v in vif_vars if v in continuous_vars and v != 'Food_Expenditure_Last_Week']
cat_vif = [v for v in vif_vars if v in categorical_vars]

# Subset and drop NaNs
df_subset = df[cont_vif + cat_vif].dropna()

# Dummy encode categorical variables
df_dummies = pd.get_dummies(df_subset, columns=cat_vif, drop_first=True, dtype=float)
df_dummies['intercept'] = 1.0
df_dummies = df_dummies.astype(float)

# Calculate VIF

vif_data["Variable"] = df_dummies.columns
vif_data["VIF"] = [variance_inflation_factor(df_dummies.values, i) for i in range(df_dummies.shape[1])]
vif_df = vif_data.sort_values(by="VIF", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

print("=" * 60)
print("1. VIF ANALYSIS")

# =============================================================
# 2 MODELS (JOURNAL STANDARD)
# =============================================================

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from linearmodels.panel import PanelOLS
import warnings

# 1. PANEL SETUP
df_panel = df.set_index(['State', 'Year'])

# 2. CONTROLS (no duplicate fafh_tax_rate)
categorical_controls = [
    "C(Marriage)", "C(Education)", "C(Employment)", "C(Living_Quarter_Status)",
    "C(Metropolitan_Status)", "C(Citizenship)", "C(Poverty)", "C(Race)"
]

# NOTE: fafh_tax_rate is kept OUT of controls_str (appear only once in formulas)
continuous_controls = ["Age", "Children"] 
controls_str = " + ".join(categorical_controls + continuous_controls)

# 3. MODEL FORMULAS

# FE-OLS baseline
twfe_formula = (
    f"Log_Food_Expenditure_Last_Week ~ 1 + fafh_tax_rate + fah_tax_rate +{controls_str}"
    f" + EntityEffects + TimeEffects"
)

# One-way FE robustness
oneway_formula = (
    f"Log_Food_Expenditure_Last_Week ~ 1 + fafh_tax_rate + fah_tax_rate + {controls_str}"
    f" + EntityEffects"
)

# 4. ESTIMATION (no IV2SLS since instruments are weak)
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
    
    # FE-OLS (baseline, not IV)
    res_twfe = PanelOLS.from_formula(
        twfe_formula, data=df_panel, drop_absorbed=True
    ).fit(cov_type='clustered', cluster_entity=True)

    res_oneway = PanelOLS.from_formula(
        oneway_formula, data=df_panel, drop_absorbed=True
    ).fit(cov_type='clustered', cluster_entity=True)

# 6. OUTPUT (SHOW ALL VARIABLES)

_BOLD = '\033[1m'
_RESET = '\033[0m'

def _print_full(result, title):
    print("\n" + "="*90)
    print(title)
    print("="*90)
    print(f"{'Variable':<45} {'Coef':>10} {'(SE)':>12} {'t-stat':>10} {'p-val':>10}")
    print("-"*90)

    for pname in sorted(result.params.index):
        coef = result.params[pname]
        se = result.std_errors[pname]
        t = result.tstats[pname]
        p = result.pvalues[pname]

        stars = '***' if p < 0.01 else '**' if p < 0.05 else '*' if p < 0.10 else ''

        print(f"{pname:<45} {coef:>10.4f} ({se:>10.4f}) {t:>10.3f} {p:>10.4f} {stars}")

    print("-"*90)
    print(f"R²: {result.rsquared:.4f}   Observations: {int(result.nobs):,}")

# PRINT ALL MODELS
_print_full(res_twfe,   "FE-OLS (TWFE)")
_print_full(res_oneway, "ONE-WAY FE (Robustness)")

# =============================================================
# TWFE MODEL WITH POVERTY INTERACTIONS — REGRESSIVITY TEST
# =============================================================
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from linearmodels.panel import PanelOLS
import warnings

# 1. LOAD YOUR FINAL, CLEANED DATA
df = pd.read_csv('final_panel_with_taxes.csv')

# 2. PANEL SETUP
df_panel = df.set_index(['State', 'Year'])

# 3. CONTROLS
categorical_controls = [
    "C(Marriage)", "C(Education)", "C(Employment)", "C(Living_Quarter_Status)",
    "C(Metropolitan_Status)", "C(Citizenship)", "C(Race)", "C(Poverty)"
]
continuous_controls = ["Age", "Children"]
controls_str = " + ".join(categorical_controls + continuous_controls)

# 4. MODEL FORMULAS — WITH poverty interactions (this tests regressivity)
twfe_formula = (
    f"Log_Food_Expenditure_Last_Week ~ 1 + fafh_tax_rate + fah_tax_rate "
    f"+ fafh_tax_rate:C(Poverty) + fah_tax_rate:C(Poverty) + {controls_str}"
    f" + EntityEffects + TimeEffects"
)

oneway_formula = (
    f"Log_Food_Expenditure_Last_Week ~ 1 + fafh_tax_rate + fah_tax_rate "
    f"+ fafh_tax_rate:C(Poverty) + fah_tax_rate:C(Poverty) + {controls_str}"
    f" + EntityEffects"
)

# 5. ESTIMATION
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

    res_twfe = PanelOLS.from_formula(
        twfe_formula, data=df_panel, drop_absorbed=True
    ).fit(cov_type='clustered', cluster_entity=True)

    res_oneway = PanelOLS.from_formula(
        oneway_formula, data=df_panel, drop_absorbed=True
    ).fit(cov_type='clustered', cluster_entity=True)

# 6. OUTPUT FUNCTION
def _print_full(result, title):
    print("\n" + "="*90)
    print(title)
    print("="*90)
    print(f"{'Variable':<45} {'Coef':>10} {'(SE)':>12} {'t-stat':>10} {'p-val':>10}")
    print("-"*90)
    for pname in sorted(result.params.index):
        coef = result.params[pname]
        se = result.std_errors[pname]
        t = result.tstats[pname]
        p = result.pvalues[pname]
        stars = '***' if p < 0.01 else '**' if p < 0.05 else '*' if p < 0.10 else ''
        print(f"{pname:<45} {coef:>10.4f} ({se:>10.4f}) {t:>10.3f} {p:>10.4f} {stars}")
    print("-"*90)
    print(f"R²: {result.rsquared:.4f}   Observations: {int(result.nobs):,}")

# 7. PRINT RESULTS
_print_full(res_twfe, "TWFE — Tax Rates x Poverty Interaction (Main Model)")
_print_full(res_oneway, "One-way FE (Robustness)")

# 8. DIRECTLY PULL OUT THE KEY REGRESSIVITY COEFFICIENTS
print("\n" + "="*90)
print("KEY REGRESSIVITY RESULTS (TWFE Main Model)")
print("="*90)
for pname in ['fafh_tax_rate', 'fah_tax_rate', 
              'fafh_tax_rate:C(Poverty)[T.2.0]', 'fah_tax_rate:C(Poverty)[T.2.0]']:
    if pname in res_twfe.params.index:
        coef = res_twfe.params[pname]
        se = res_twfe.std_errors[pname]
        p = res_twfe.pvalues[pname]
        print(f"{pname:<45} coef={coef:.4f}  se={se:.4f}  p={p:.4f}")

  # =============================================================
  # F-TEST FOR TIME FIXED EFFECTS (Chapter 6 requirement)
  # H0: All year dummies are jointly zero
  # =============================================================
  import numpy as np

  r2_twfe   = res_twfe.rsquared
  r2_oneway = res_oneway.rsquared
  nobs      = int(res_twfe.nobs)
  T         = df['Year'].nunique()       # number of time periods
  k         = len(res_twfe.params)       # regressors in TWFE

  q      = T - 1                         # time dummies (one normalised out)
  df_err = nobs - k - 1
  delta_r2 = r2_twfe - r2_oneway
  F_time   = (delta_r2 / q) / ((1 - r2_twfe) / df_err)

  print("=" * 60)
  print("F-TEST FOR TIME FIXED EFFECTS")
  print("H0: All year dummies are jointly zero")
  print("=" * 60)
  print(f"R² TWFE (with time FE):   {r2_twfe:.4f}")
  print(f"R² One-Way FE (no time):  {r2_oneway:.4f}")
  print(f"Delta R²:                 {delta_r2:.4f}")
  print(f"q (time dummies):         {q}")
  print(f"F-statistic:              {F_time:.4f}")
  print()
  if F_time > 2.5:
      print("Conclusion: Time effects JOINTLY SIGNIFICANT → TWFE is correct specification.")
      print("One-Way FE (Table 7) is a robustness check only — biased if used as main result.")
  else:
      print("Conclusion: Time effects NOT significant → One-Way FE may be sufficient.")
